learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the harsh reality of child labor, extreme poverty, and how the 'spring' (childhood) of millions of children is lost in the slums of India.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Saheb is a ragpicker whose family migrated from Dhaka to Seemapuri (Delhi) due to storms. Ironically, his name means 'Lord of the Universe', but he roams barefoot searching for 'gold' in garbage dumps.

main_concepts.concept_title: 👟 The Illusion of the Tea Stall
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Saheb eventually gets a job at a tea stall. Though he earns 800 rupees and all his meals, he loses his 'carefree look'. The steel canister belongs to the master; he is no longer his own master.
Mukesh belongs to a family of bangle makers in Firozabad. Unlike others who accept their fate (karma), Mukesh dares to dream of becoming a motor mechanic and driving a car.
The bangle makers are trapped in a vicious web of poverty created by the sahukars (moneylenders), middlemen, policemen, bureaucrats, and politicians. They cannot organize a cooperative.
Children and adults work in glass furnaces with high temperatures and dingy cells without air or light. Many end up losing their eyesight before they become adults.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Name Irony
fun_activity.instructions: Saheb's full name is 'Saheb-e-Alam' (Lord of the Universe), but he is a poor ragpicker. Think of a famous fictional character whose name is the complete opposite of their personality or situation!

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast the two boys: Saheb gives up his freedom for a job, while Mukesh insists on breaking tradition to achieve his dream of being a mechanic.
📌 Explain what garbage means to them: For elders, it's a means of survival. For children, it is wrapped in wonder (they might find a coin).
📌 Use the term 'Vicious Circle of Middlemen' when explaining why the bangle makers of Firozabad remain perpetually poor.
quick_recap: ⭐ The title 'Lost Spring' is a metaphor: Spring is the season of joy and growth (childhood), which these children never get to experience.
⭐ Seemapuri is geographically close to Delhi, but metaphorically miles away from its development and privileges.
⭐ Mukesh's dream of flying an airplane is a step too far for him; he is content dreaming about cars.
